summary: BBN announces a change to how IMPs report status. Text status reports would be removed, since a binary version sent straight to the Network Control Center had already replaced them. The remaining reports from the statistics program would no longer be affected by host parameter-change settings, so hosts cannot accidentally interfere with network monitoring.

plainLanguage.summary: The people watching the network are getting rid of an old paper-style report that nobody needs, and making sure other users cannot change the settings of their monitoring gadget by accident.

subtitle: Notification of changes to IMP status reporting to the Network Control Center

tldr.problem: The IMP system had two forms of status reporting: text-based messages that were generated per-host and a binary format sent directly to the Network Control Center. The text reports had become redundant since the binary version superseded them.
tldr.mechanism: BBN removes the text status reports entirely, keeping only the binary version that goes to the NCC. The remaining statistics program on fake host 3 is modified to no longer respond to host parameter-change settings, preventing hosts from accidentally interfering with NCC monitoring.
tldr.outcome: The IMP reporting system becomes simpler, with less excess data, and the NCC's monitoring is protected from unintended host interference.

today: This change exemplified good network operations practice: centralizing monitoring, removing redundancy, and protecting critical infrastructure from unintended user interference.

sections.title: Status Reporting Change
sections.content:
To help BBN expand its role as the Network Control Center, changes were made to the IMP's status reporting facility. The primary change was removing text-based status reports that had become redundant.

The text reports had already been completely superseded by a binary version sent directly to the NCC. The text reports were now excess baggage consuming unnecessary bandwidth and resources, so BBN removed them from the system within one month of this announcement.
sections.plainLanguage: The network managers decide to stop sending old-fashioned text reports because they already have a better computer-readable version.

sections.title: Statistics Program Protection
sections.content:
The status reports through the statistics program on fake host 3 are retained, but a key change is made: these reports will no longer be affected by any PARAMETER CHANGE directives issued by hosts. This isolation prevents hosts from inadvertently or intentionally interfering with the Network Control Center's monitoring operations.

By decoupling the statistics program from host parameter changes, the NCC gains reliable visibility into network status without risk that host software might alter monitoring behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: The monitoring stays where it is, but host computers cannot change its settings by accident.

sections.title: Impact
sections.content: These changes are expected to be transparent to hosts, requiring no host software modifications. The removal of redundant text reports simplifies the IMP implementation and reduces network traffic. The isolation of monitoring from host parameter changes increases the reliability and security of NCC operations.
sections.plainLanguage: Host computers will not notice the change, but the network monitoring becomes simpler and safer.
